name: VOD Episode Sweep
description: Learns which VOD series a client syncs and refreshes ALL of each watched show's provider/category relations so new episodes stop going missing. Scoped to only the series you sync; runs in the background.
author: andyj682

fields.label: Prioritize refresh by airing status
fields.help_text: Refresh shows that are airing every day, and everything else on a rotation (plus anything new, carried over, or reported changed by its provider). Most watched shows aren't airing, so this cuts the daily provider load sharply. Off = refresh every watched show every day, as before 1.2.0.

fields.label: Refresh when a provider reports a change
fields.help_text: Refresh a show the day its provider's listing says it changed since the last refresh, whatever its airing status. Catches what no schedule shows: a new copy of an old show, backfilled seasons, fixed episodes. Ignored for a provider that marks most of its listing changed at once. Default on.

fields.label: TMDB API key (optional)
fields.help_text: A free TMDB key (v3 API key or v4 read access token) lets the plugin follow each show's airing schedule: refreshed daily around new episodes, and from a few days before a new season starts. Only TMDB ids are sent. Without a key, stored episode air dates are used instead. Falls back to Dispatcharr's TMDB_API_KEY environment variable if that is set.

fields.label: Auto-run daily sweep
fields.help_text: Automatically run the daily sweep on a timer at the hour below. When off, it still runs -- but only when a client next requests a series after that hour, which lags new episodes by an extra sync. Leave on unless you have a reason not to.

fields.label: Earliest sweep hour (0-23)
fields.help_text: Hour the daily sweep runs, in Dispatcharr's configured system timezone. With Auto-run daily sweep on (above), a timer fires the sweep at this hour; otherwise it fires on the first client series request at/after this hour. Set it a bit BEFORE your client's daily sync so new episodes are ready in one pass. Default 3.

fields.label: Auto-retry stale relations
fields.help_text: After each sweep, keep re-refreshing whatever is still flagged stale until nothing is, then stop. A provider that stays down (about 90 minutes) or makes no progress is given up for the day, and the rest carry on. Does nothing on a clean day.

fields.label: Max retry passes per day
fields.help_text: Upper limit on automatic retry passes per day (0-24). The chain normally stops well before this, as soon as nothing is stale. 0 turns auto-retry off. Default 12.

fields.label: Quiet window for retries (optional)
fields.help_text: Optional time range, like 09:55-10:15, when automatic retries make no provider calls: a pass due inside it waits until it ends. Use it to keep retries out of your client's library sync. Empty = none.

fields.label: Airing window (days)
fields.help_text: How long after an episode airs (per TMDB) a show stays on the daily refresh. Covers providers that post episodes late. Default 10.

fields.label: Rotation for other shows (days)
fields.help_text: Shows that aren't airing are still refreshed at least once every this many days (1-28), spread evenly across the days. Lower = fresher, more provider calls. Default 7.

fields.label: Fallback airing window (days)
fields.help_text: For shows without usable TMDB data: refreshed daily while a stored episode air date (or a newly appeared episode) is within this many days. Default 14.

fields.label: Watchlist TTL (days)
fields.help_text: A series leaves the watchlist only after this many days unseen AND after your client has ignored 3 refreshes of it (or after 120 days unseen regardless), so a show refreshed only weekly, or whose provider is having a bad week, isn't dropped while you still follow it. Default 30.

fields.label: Refresh batch size
fields.help_text: Series per background refresh task. Smaller batches spread the provider get_series_info calls into smaller bursts (gentler on provider rate limits). 0 = one task per account. Default 20.

fields.label: Refresh spacing (seconds)
fields.help_text: Delay inserted between successive refresh batches (via a Celery countdown) so they don't all hit the providers at once. 0 = fire everything immediately. Default 15.

fields.label: Schedule queue (advanced)
fields.help_text: Advanced: the Celery queue the scheduled sweep is dispatched to. It must be served by a worker that loads plugins -- on a stock Dispatcharr that's the threads-pool 'dvr' worker (the default prefork worker rejects plugin tasks). Change only if your worker layout differs. If the scheduled sweep never runs, the opportunistic trigger still covers it.

fields.description: The watchlist is built automatically by observing the series your client requests over the XC API -- no manual list needed. A 'watchlist_debug.json' file is written in this plugin's folder (under data/plugins/) during each refresh. Only Xtream-Codes VOD series are affected.

actions.label: Show status
actions.description: Report whether the patch is active, the schedule, and the watchlist size.

actions.label: List watched series
actions.description: Show the series currently on the watchlist and the path to the debug JSON file.

actions.label: Run sweep now
actions.description: Run the episode sweep now, regardless of the daily timer.

actions.label: Retry stale relations
actions.description: Retry only relations still flagged stale.

actions.label: Update TMDB schedules
actions.description: Look up airing schedules on TMDB now.

actions.label: Clear watchlist
actions.description: Forget every watched series. It will be rebuilt as clients request series again.

confirm.title: Clear the watchlist?
confirm.message: This removes every remembered series. It rebuilds automatically as clients sync series again.
